application_questions.question: An L-shaped courtyard has outer dimensions $14\text{ m}$ by $10\text{ m}$, with a rectangular corner measuring $6\text{ m}$ by $4\text{ m}$ removed. Find (a) the perimeter of the courtyard and (b) the area of the courtyard.

A rectangular picture measuring $40\text{ cm}$ by $30\text{ cm}$ is surrounded by a timber frame of uniform width $5\text{ cm}$ on all sides. Find the outer dimensions of the frame and the area of the timber frame itself.
application_questions.answer: Outer dimensions $50\text{ cm} \times 40\text{ cm}$; frame area $= 800\text{ cm}^2$

application_questions.question: A wheat farm in the Wimmera consists of a rectangular paddock of $600\text{ m}$ by $400\text{ m}$ joined to a triangular paddock of base $400\text{ m}$ and perpendicular height $300\text{ m}$. Find the total area of the farm in square metres and in hectares.
A kite-shaped stunt sail has diagonals of lengths $2.4\text{ m}$ and $1.5\text{ m}$. If ripstop nylon fabric costs $\$35$ per square metre, what is the cost of the fabric needed to make the sail?

reasoning_questions.question: A parallelogram and a triangle have the exact same base length $b$ and the exact same area $A$. How does the perpendicular height of the triangle compare to the perpendicular height of the parallelogram? Justify your answer algebraically.
reasoning_questions.answer: The triangle's height must be twice the parallelogram's height ($h_{\text{tri}} = 2h_{\text{para}}$), since $\frac{1}{2}bh_{\text{tri}} = bh_{\text{para}} \implies h_{\text{tri}} = 2h_{\text{para}}$.

reasoning_questions.question: Every staircase L-shape cut from the corner of a $W \times H$ rectangle has the same perimeter $2(W + H)$ as the original rectangle. Explain why removing a rectangular corner decreases the area but leaves the perimeter unchanged.
reasoning_questions.answer: The horizontal and vertical inner step edges equal the removed top and side edges in length, so the total boundary length stays $2(W + H)$.

application_questions.question: A circular cricket oval in Melbourne has a boundary radius of $70\text{ m}$. Using $\pi \approx \dfrac{22}{7}$, find (a) the length of the boundary fence around the oval and (b) the turf area of the oval in square metres and in hectares.

A circular pond of radius $4\text{ m}$ is surrounded by a gravel path of width $2\text{ m}$ (forming an outer radius of $6\text{ m}$). Find the exact area of the gravel path in terms of $\pi$, and round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
A windscreen wiper blade of length $45\text{ cm}$ sweeps through an angle of $120^\circ$ from its pivot. Find the exact area of glass cleaned in a single sweep in terms of $\pi$.

A rectangular sheet of steel measuring $20\text{ cm}$ by $10\text{ cm}$ has two identical largest-possible circles of diameter $10\text{ cm}$ ($r = 5\text{ cm}$) stamped out of it. Find the exact area of steel remaining.

reasoning_questions.question: A piece of wire of length $44\text{ cm}$ is bent into a square, and an identical $44\text{ cm}$ wire is bent into a circle. Using $\pi \approx \dfrac{22}{7}$, find the area of both shapes and determine which shape encloses the larger area.
reasoning_questions.answer: Square side $= 11\text{ cm} \implies A_{\text{square}} = 121\text{ cm}^2$; Circle radius $= 7\text{ cm} \implies A_{\text{circle}} = 154\text{ cm}^2$. The circle encloses $33\text{ cm}^2$ more area.

reasoning_questions.question: If the circumference of a circle is $16\pi\text{ cm}$, show how to work backwards to find its radius $r$ and then its exact area $A$.

application_questions.question: A rectangular garden Lap Pool in Echuca is $15\text{ m}$ long, $3\text{ m}$ wide, and has a uniform depth of $1.4\text{ m}$. Calculate (a) its volume in $\text{m}^3$ and (b) its capacity in litres ($\text{L}$).

A wedge of Gippsland cheddar cheese is shaped like a right triangular prism with a right-angled triangle base of legs $9\text{ cm}$ and $12\text{ cm}$ and a thickness of $6\text{ cm}$. Find the volume of the cheese wedge in $\text{cm}^3$.

During January (Daylight Saving), Sydney is on AEDT (UTC$+11$) and Brisbane is on AEST (UTC$+10$). A flight departs Sydney at $8{:}20\text{ am}$ AEDT and takes $1\text{ hour } 35\text{ minutes}$ to reach Brisbane. What is the local arrival time in Brisbane (AEST)?
application_questions.answer: $8{:}55\text{ am}$ AEST ($9{:}55\text{ am}$ AEDT minus $1\text{ hour}$)

application_questions.question: A rectangular rainwater tank has a base measuring $2.5\text{ m}$ by $1.6\text{ m}$. When $6000\text{ L}$ ($6\text{ m}^3$) of water is pumped into the empty tank, to what depth $h$ (in metres) does the water rise?

reasoning_questions.question: A solid metal cube of side length $10\text{ cm}$ is submerged completely inside a rectangular tank of base area $250\text{ cm}^2$ partially filled with water. By how many centimetres does the water level rise? Show your reasoning.
reasoning_questions.answer: $4\text{ cm}$, since the cube displaces $10^3 = 1000\text{ cm}^3$ of water, and $\Delta h = \dfrac{1000}{250} = 4\text{ cm}$.

reasoning_questions.question: A live cricket test match in Perth starts at $10{:}30\text{ am}$ AWST (UTC$+8$). Explain why viewers in Melbourne watching in December (AEDT, UTC$+11$) see the first ball bowled at $1{:}30\text{ pm}$, whereas if it were played in winter (AEST, UTC$+10$) they would see it at $12{:}30\text{ pm}$.
reasoning_questions.answer: In winter Melbourne is $2$ hours ahead of Perth ($10 - 8 = 2$), whereas in December Melbourne observes Daylight Saving (UTC$+11$) while WA does not, making the difference $11 - 8 = 3$ hours.
